title: Prediction: Colette Kress Is More Vital to Nvidia’s Future Than Her Interim CEO Title Implies
author: Daniel Foelber
description: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO due to personal scandals, CFO Colette Kress has assumed the interim CEO role. The article argues that Kress, who has historically balanced Huang's visionary but risky bets with financial discipline, may fundamentally shift Nvidia's strategy toward a more cautious approach. This could slow growth but reduce vulnerability to AI spending downturns, potentially transforming Nvidia from a high-growth stock into a value-oriented investment.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the leadership transition creates uncertainty and near-term volatility, the article suggests Kress's more disciplined approach could benefit long-term investors by reducing risky bets and maintaining high margins. The stock is down significantly, but the fundamental business remains strong with potential for steady compounding rather than boom-bust cycles.

title: If You Have $1,000 to Invest in December, These 3 Stocks Are Built to Last a Decade
author: Rick Orford
description: The article recommends three tech stocks for long-term investors: Microsoft, ASML, and TSMC. Microsoft benefits from its integrated ecosystem and AI-driven cloud growth with Azure revenue up 48% YoY. ASML dominates semiconductor lithography equipment with hard-to-replicate competitive advantages. TSMC leads in advanced chip manufacturing with 51% YoY revenue growth. All three are positioned to capitalize on AI demand over the next decade, though each carries specific risks including geopolitical tensions and cyclical spending.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong ecosystem moat, 48% Azure revenue growth YoY, multiple AI monetization paths through Copilot and cloud infrastructure. Wall Street average target implies 21% upside. Described as 'safest option' with reasonable 26x forward P/E valuation.

Extremely difficult-to-replicate competitive advantage in lithography equipment, record Q3 net sales of €11.7B, customers already placing orders for 2029-2030. Wall Street consensus suggests 50% upside with reasonable 23x forward P/E. Positioned as middle-risk option.

Dominant foundry business with 51% YoY revenue growth, 79% of wafer revenue from advanced technologies, strong two-nanometer ramp. 20 of 21 analysts rate buy/strong buy with 57% upside potential. Attractive 18x forward P/E valuation, though characterized as higher-risk due to China-Taiwan tensions.

title: Nebius Posted Superb Earnings and Crashed Anyway. Buy the Dip.
author: Marc Guberti
description: Nebius stock fell 17% after earnings despite strong fundamentals, primarily due to a delay in reaching $7-9 billion ARR targets from December 2026 to February 2027. The delay stems from colocation facility issues rather than execution problems. The company's business model continues to strengthen with rising megawatt values ($25M+ per megawatt in Q3), improving payback periods, and 75-85% of 2027 capex expected to be covered by prepayments. The analyst views the stock decline as a buying opportunity for long-term investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite a 17% stock decline post-earnings, the article highlights strong underlying fundamentals including rising megawatt values, improving payback periods, strong customer prepayments covering capex, and a shift away from risky colocation models. The ARR delay is characterized as a minor timing issue rather than a structural problem, with the analyst recommending the dip as a buying opportunity.

Microsoft is mentioned as a major customer with a $17.4 billion, five-year infrastructure deal with Nebius. The delay in capacity availability is attributed to Microsoft's colocation facility, not Microsoft's performance or strategy. No direct sentiment about Microsoft's business is expressed.

title: Is the Stock Market Really in an AI Bubble? Wall Street's Doomsayers Are Ignoring Crucial Facts.
author: Trevor Jennewine
description: While prominent Wall Street bears warn of an AI bubble and potential market crash, the article argues their concerns overlook key facts. The S&P 500's forward price-to-earnings ratio has fallen to its lowest level in three years as earnings growth accelerates, contrasting with the dot-com bubble. AI adoption is outpacing previous technological revolutions with measurable productivity gains, suggesting the boom has genuine economic benefits rather than being purely speculative.

title: Eviden étend à Microsoft Azure sa solution de gestion souveraine des clés cryptographiques
author: Eviden/Atos Group
description: Eviden announces new capabilities enabling organizations to maintain full control over encryption keys while using Microsoft Azure. The solution offers two deployment models: keeping cryptographic infrastructure outside Azure under customer control, or running Eviden KMS in a confidential virtual machine on Azure while maintaining Proteccio HSM as an external sovereign root of trust. This allows customers to leverage Azure's cloud performance while preserving data sovereignty and cryptographic control.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Microsoft Azure benefits from this partnership by offering enhanced security and sovereignty features through external key management capabilities, making Azure more attractive to organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements.

As the parent company of Eviden, Atos benefits from the expansion of its cybersecurity product portfolio and demonstrates leadership in sovereign cloud security solutions, strengthening its position as a European cybersecurity leader.
